intro: Haikou rewards visitors with historic arcade streets, volcanic parks and fresh seafood by the strait. Pick how long you have and what you enjoy most.
tour_note: Check the tour page for which entry tickets are included.

notes: No metro; commuter trains on the Hainan high-speed line link the airport and main stations.
City buses are cheap and cover most routes; fares are a few yuan.
Taxis meter from about ¥10; insist on the meter (dabiao).
Ride-hailing apps DiDi and Amap work well; Uber does not operate.
Bikes and electric scooters are easy to rent; riverside paths are good.
Ferries cross to Xuwen and Beihai from New Port and Xiuying Port.

qilou.name: Qilou Old Street
qilou.price_text: Free to walk · small fees for some houses
qilou.tip: Come in the late afternoon when the arcades shade the walk and the snack stalls open.

century_bridge.name: Haikou Century Bridge
century_bridge.tip: Walk or cycle the bridge at sunset for the best light over the strait.

qiongzhou.name: Qiongzhou Strait
qiongzhou.price_text: Free to view · ferry fares vary, check on the day
qiongzhou.hours: Always open · ferries run by timetable
qiongzhou.tip: View it from the west coast beaches or the bridge; ferries to the mainland leave from the port.

qilou_snacks.name: Bo'ai Old Street snack lanes
qilou_snacks.tip: Try Hainan coconut rice and grilled seafood; point at what looks busy with locals.

wugongci.name: Wugong Ci (Five Officials Temple)
wugongci.tip: A quiet garden temple honouring officials exiled to Hainan; good for an hour out of the sun.

bihai_park.name: Bihai Avenue coastal walk
bihai_park.tip: A long seafront promenade for walking or cycling; rent a shared bike and head west.

holiday_beach.name: Holiday Beach (West Coast)
holiday_beach.price_text: Free · sunbeds and showers cost extra
holiday_beach.hours: Always open · swimming in daylight hours
holiday_beach.tip: Sandy and family-friendly; watch for jellyfish in summer and check flags on the day.

volcano_park.name: Haikou Volcanic Cluster Geopark
volcano_park.tip: Half a day out of town to walk old lava fields and crater trails; bring water and sun cover.

hainan_museum.name: Hainan Provincial Museum
hainan_museum.tip: Good rainy-day stop for Hainan history and minority culture; bring your passport.

wanlv_park.name: Wanlv Garden
wanlv_park.tip: Shaded city park with coconut palms; a calm break between old street and museum.

night_market.name: Haikou night food market
night_market.tip: Go hungry and share plates; seafood is priced by weight, so ask before ordering.

coconut_drink.name: Fresh coconut and Hainan coffee stop
coconut_drink.tip: Hainan coffee is served strong and sweet; pair it with a chilled coconut.

meilan_beach.name: Meilan coastal area
meilan_beach.tip: Quieter beaches near the airport side; good if you have time before a flight.

airport_garden.name: Meilan airport garden stop
airport_garden.tip: Green space near the terminal for a short walk if you arrive early.

ferry_view.name: Ferry port viewpoint
ferry_view.price_text: Free to watch · ferry tickets vary
ferry_view.tip: Watch the strait ferries load; check sailing times on the day if you plan to cross.

old_street_walk.name: Arcade architecture walk
old_street_walk.tip: Look up at the weathered facades above the shops; go early to avoid crowds.

seafood_dinner.name: Seafood dinner by the strait
seafood_dinner.tip: Pick your fish from the tank and agree the price per weight first.

bike_ride.name: West Coast bike ride
bike_ride.tip: Ride the seafront path from the bridge westward; flat and easy.

temple_street.name: Neighbourhood lane walk
temple_street.tip: Wander the small lanes behind the old street for local life and tea houses.

stays.why: Walk to the arcaded old streets, snack stalls and small temples. Central for buses and taxis.
Downtown shopping and food, close to the museum and easy taxi pickups.
Beach resorts and long seaside walks; quieter nights, farther from the old town.
Closest to the airport and the high-speed train station; handy for early flights.

food: Try Hainan staples: Wenchang chicken, coconut rice, and a bowl of Hainan-style noodles for breakfast.
Seafood: pick fish and shellfish at a market or tank restaurant and have it cooked; agree the price per weight first.
Street snacks around Bo'ai Old Street: coconut water, grilled squid and sweet rice cakes, mostly ¥5–20.
Cool down with qingbuliang, a sweet coconut-milk dessert soup with beans and fruit.
Big night food streets and open-air seafood places get busy after 7pm; go early or expect a wait.
more_time: Add a day trip to the volcanic crater park and lava villages north of the city; check opening hours on the day.
Take the high-speed train to Sanya for beaches and resort life, roughly 1.5–2 hours each way.
Slow down on the West Coast: a sunset walk, a beach café and an evening seafood dinner.
